new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is fixed on the penultimate syllable of the word, where the word excludes the paragogic (echo) vowel that follows a root-final consonant (buok+u 'hair' etc.). A sequence of identical vowels in the antepenult+penult is stressed on its first mora (maata), i.e. a long vowel counts as one heavy penult (Wikipedia paraphrases this as 'a sequence of like vowels counts as one syllable'). Stress is recomputed on the suffixed/cliticised word, so suffixes and enclitics shift stress rightward (bolé-ku, noitamó=lon); when a suffix or enclitic is added the paragogic vowel is dropped and stress is regular penult.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in the snippets retrieved.
new_statements.exceptions: Paragogic vowels are extrametrical (not counted); like-vowel sequences across antepenult/penult take stress on the antepenultimate mora; enclitics and suffixes shift stress to the right. The 2010 Survey (citing Sneddon & Usup 1986: 418) adds that the paragogic vowel is being lost in Buol, which yields regular penult stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological word including suffixes and enclitics (stress shifts with them); paragogic vowel excluded from the count. Citation-form vs phrase-level behaviour not discussed in the snippets.
new_statements.identity_note: Zobel 2005 describes Buol proper (apadu Vuolo, Kabupaten Buol, c. 75,000 speakers per Grimes 1996) = buol1237; no dialect is singled out. Access caveat: the deciding sentences come from Google Books full-text search snippets of the Routledge chapter (three overlapping snippets reconstruct the passage word for word), not from an open PDF or a held scan; the feed exposes no page number. The full chapter remains paywalled; if a stricter standard is required, downgrade to a description exists but is not accessible and keep the quote as provisional.

new_statements.quote: p. 418: "Loss of the paragogic vowel but not etymological vowel in word-final position can probably be accounted for in terms of stress placement. Stress in Bul falls on the penult unless there is a paragogic vowel, in which case it falls on the antepenult. Loss of the paragogic syllable in Bul therefore results in regular penult stress.15" -- fn. 15 (p. 425): "The Holle list (Stokhof 1983:139-181) shows stress placement in Bul. This is identical with the word stress pattern in Kdp. It is probable that in pre-PGtl stress regularly feil [sic, = fell] on the penult. With the development of the paragogic vowel stress thus became unpredictable (as in Kdp and, until this change, in Bul). In Gtl stress again became regular by shifting from the antepenult to the penult in words containing a paragogic syllable."

new_statements.relation_note: Same placement as the catalog record (penult in every word length: penultimate stress) and as the existing Zobel 2005 statement ('Stress regularly falls on the penultimate syllable, paragogic vowels not counted'). Sneddon & Usup state the identical rule from the diachronic side (penult, paragogic syllable extrametrical, hence antepenult on the surface where the vowel survives). It also confirms first-hand the wording that van der Hulst, Goedemans & van Zanten 2010 attribute to 'Sneddon and Usup 1986: 418'. No contradiction; it adds no synchronic detail beyond Zobel, so 'agrees' rather than 'refines'.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress in Buol falls on the penultimate syllable; in words that (still) end in the paragogic vowel (historically *o added after an originally final consonant) stress stays on the etymological penult, i.e. surfaces on the antepenult -- the paragogic syllable does not count. Since the paragogic vowel is being lost in Buol (84 of 97 relevant items in the authors' eastern-dialect list), the outcome is regular penultimate stress. The footnote adds that the Buol pattern in the 1919 Holle list is identical to Kaidipang's and calls surface stress 'unpredictable' only in the sense that penult vs antepenult depends on whether the final vowel is paragogic.
new_statements.exceptions: Only the paragogic-vowel condition (antepenult surface stress when a paragogic vowel is present; the vowel is retained morphophonemically before consonant-initial enclitics such as -po 'still', p. 417). Nothing on like-vowel sequences, enclitic/suffix stress shift, or secondary stress (those details are Zobel 2005's).
new_statements.identity_note: The article's 'Bul' is Buol proper (buol1237), 'the most westerly of the Gorontalic languages.. in the extreme north-east district of the Province of Central Sulawesi' (p. 409); the authors' own 200-item list is from a village in the EAST of the Buol-speaking area, compared with Barr, Barr & Salombe's (1979) list from the west, and they note paragogic-vowel loss is further advanced in the eastern dialect (pp. 417-418). Footnote 3 (p. 425) warns that of the two 'Buol' lists in Stokhof 1983 only pp. 139-181 is actually Buol.
